name: Acts of Gathering
description:
Police Violence on a Group of Satyagrahis, Gifted by Roopa & G.V. Ravi Shankar
This photograph from India, 1930 shows a group of satyagrahis interlocking their arms, as the force of a colonial police officer attempts to break apart this protest. We do not know where this photograph was specifically taken or what protest they were a part of; and yet the strength of a collective gathering is evident. Several images such as this reflect the mass nature of the Indian independence movement. People from different walks of life, even with differing ideologies and social positions, united for the common cause of independence. 

Imagine the moments before and after this photograph was taken. What brought these people together? How did they hear about this protest? Did they anticipate the violent repression that they eventually faced? What happened to them after this moment, were they injured or arrested? Did they continue to protest despite the violence, or was the call to gather amplified by it? Are these photographs just a memory of the past or do they hold a mirror to a reality of the present? Is this photograph bound by time or does it continue to inform and inspire?

Photographs such as these and other archival documents implore us to look beyond the iconic and popular imagery of the independence movement. They also give us an opportunity to engage with the idea of gatherings, their particular contexts in Indian history and beyond.

In this two-day workshop, Acts of Gathering, visual artist Uzma Mohsin will take participants through photographs, documents, and other visual material from the Gandhi Collection. Participants will engage with Mohsin’s own work on photographs, archives, and public histories. They will think through the idea of political gatherings and develop a response to the material in the collection.

name: Invisible Inks
description:
In the second edition of Shared Futures, a series accompanying Beneath the Turning Sky, visual artist Rai joins curator Priya Chauhan to discuss Rai's work Crater I, on view in the exhibition. Together, they situate the piece within Rai's broader practice, drawing connections to other themes and areas of inquiry explored in Beneath the Turning Sky.

The conversation and lecture-demonstration will be followed by a hands-on workshop on invisible inks, giving participants an opportunity to engage with some of the ideas through making.

Beneath the Turning Sky brings together artists working across painting, sculpture, photography, and textile practices, illuminating contemporary debates around ecology, technology, development, and our relationship with the environment. Through distinct visual languages, the exhibition asks: How might art reshape our collective stewardship of the planet?

Extending these questions beyond the gallery, Shared Futures creates a space for exchange through lectures, conversations, workshops, and other experimental formats. Across these encounters, the series considers what the arts can offer in turbulent times and how creative practices can help forge new ways of thinking, being, and building solidarity.

This event is held in conjunction with our ongoing permanent exhibition Beneath the Turning Sky.
